elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "commits to purchase no minimum amount of Services"; the prior "at least USD 2,000,000 ... on a take-or-pay basis" is removed

elements.element: Fees are payable for usage or ordered Services only
elements.evidence: "and pays only for Services ordered or used"

elements.element: Commitment limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: clause retains "in each of the next three years" and states no 12-month commitment period
no notice-based reduction right appears in the rendered clause

elements.element: True-up rather than a penalty for shortfall
elements.evidence: no shortfall or true-up mechanic in the rendered clause (take-or-pay simply deleted)

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the monetary minimum and the take-or-pay mechanic are eliminated and fees are expressly limited to Services ordered or used.

The rewrite is confined to the single offending sentence; no free-standing reduction or termination right, fallback true-up mechanic, or other new exception was imported, so nothing exceeds what the preferred level requires.
Residual phrase "in each of the next three years" is inert once the minimum is "no minimum amount" and fees are usage-based; it creates no contradiction or dangling mechanic.
Fallback elements (12-month scope, 30-day reduction notice, true-up) are absent, which is expected and permissible because the locked target is preferred and the two levels must not be combined.
Margin comment correctly explains the change and offers the fallback without adding operative effect.
